title: GPT-5.5 Pro solves Erdős problem #38; solution human-checked, Lean-formalized and recorded as solved on erdosproblems.com
summary: GPT-5.5 Pro solved Erdős problem #38; on 1 May 2026 the Aristotle system formalized the proof in Lean, and erdosproblems.com records the problem as solved.
account: Erdős problem #38 was an open question in additive number theory. It asks for a set B that is not an additive basis yet raises the Schnirelmann density of every set A. OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Pro solved it. On 25 April 2026 a user (gebyjaff) posted the model's solution on the erdosproblems.com forum, with a PDF cleanup by Liam Price. On 26 April forum commenter Nat Sothanaphan reported that a standard check found no issues in the write-up. On 1 May the Aristotle system autoformalized the argument in Lean, and Sothanaphan confirmed that the formalization matches the paper. The same day Terence Tao changed the status of problem 38 in the community Erdős problem database from open to proved with a Lean proof. On 2 May 2026 site maintainer Thomas Bloom posted an alternative sketch. In it he wrote that the argument is short and mostly classical, and that it is close to Ruzsa's construction of thin essential components. The problem page now records the positive solution by GPT 5.5 Pro. Terence Tao's wiki lists it as an AI-standalone full solution.
purpose: General-purpose reasoning model prompted to solve an open research problem
system: GPT-5.5 Pro, with Aristotle used for Lean autoformalisation
developer: OpenAI (GPT-5.5 Pro); Aristotle (developer not named in the cited sources)

ratings.reason: Small: one more entry resolved in the erdosproblems.com project, accepted by its maintainer

ai_role.statement: The model produced the proof after a human prompt. Humans cleaned up the write-up and checked it, and the maintainer accepted it. A separate AI system (Aristotle) produced the Lean formalization that a human confirmed matches the paper. Tao's wiki classifies the case as AI standalone with non-significant human involvement. Site maintainer Thomas Bloom writes that the argument is short and mostly classical, and that it is close to Ruzsa's construction of thin essential components. The attribution of GPT-5.5 Pro to OpenAI rests on the chatgpt.com share link in gebyjaff's forum post.

fields.account: Erdős problem #38 was an open question in additive number theory. It asks for a set B that is not an additive basis yet raises the Schnirelmann density of every set A. OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Pro solved it. On 25 April 2026 a user (gebyjaff) posted the model's solution on the erdosproblems.com forum, with a PDF cleanup by Liam Price. On 26 April forum commenter Nat Sothanaphan reported that a standard check found no issues in the write-up. On 1 May the Aristotle system autoformalized the argument in Lean, and Sothanaphan confirmed that the formalization matches the paper. The same day Terence Tao changed the status of problem 38 in the community Erdős problem database from open to proved with a Lean proof. On 2 May 2026 site maintainer Thomas Bloom posted an alternative sketch. In it he wrote that the argument is short and mostly classical, and that it is close to Ruzsa's construction of thin essential components. The problem page now records the positive solution by GPT 5.5 Pro. Terence Tao's wiki lists it as an AI-standalone full solution.
